name: Luti people
summary: Luti (Persian: لوطی) was a term used in Qajar Iran and earlier to describe a social group of men who shared certain traits in their appearance and conduct.
description: Luti (Persian: لوطی) was a term used in Qajar Iran and earlier to describe a social group of men who shared certain traits in their appearance and conduct. These included adherence to certain moral values, such as chivalry and trustworthiness, while remaining indifferent to some other moral norms. Lutis often frequented zurkhanehs, and some made a living through singing, dancing, or putting on entertainments involving monkeys or other animals. Lutis held a low social status and were even regarded by some as troublemakers or ruffians. In some contexts, the word luti also carried homosexual connotations.
